title: Lean-Verified Deterministic Subexponential Integer Factoring Bound 2^O(b/√log b)
aiSystem: Anthropic Clique Evaluator + Multi-Agent Lean Proofs (Big O Speedrun)
whyItMatters: Open-internet Big O Speedrun collaboration proved and dual-kernel Lean-verified a deterministic 2^O(b/√log b) factoring bound—turning Rudich–Rousseau Conjecture 1 into a theorem.
summary: Bridging Anthropic’s ETH clique evaluator with Isaac Rudich and Louis-Martin Rousseau’s factoring reduction, independent researchers—including high-school researcher Cinna Davis and Big O Speedrun contributors—proved in Lean 4 that deterministic integer factoring of b-bit numbers runs in time 2^O(b/√log b). The formal proof was independently checked by two separate Lean kernels (Lean + nanoda) on Big O Speedrun.
technicalHighlights: Elevated Rudich & Rousseau’s Conjecture 1 to a machine-checked unconditional deterministic complexity theorem.
Independently verified by two distinct Lean proof kernels via the open Big O Speedrun verification harness.
Exemplifies rapid, decentralized GitHub-native research combining AI-generated theorems from major labs with independent open-source contributors.
caveats: Asymptotic worst-case complexity theorem with large implicit constants; does not threaten practical RSA key sizes or beat randomized GNFS in practice.

scoreRationale.foundational: Established a major deterministic unconditional upper bound on integer factoring complexity.
scoreRationale.ripple: Showcased how open Lean leaderboards (Big O Speedrun) let independent researchers and agents compose lab breakthroughs in days.
scoreRationale.verification: Verified independently by two separate Lean kernels with standard axioms only.
scoreRationale.velocity: Assembled, formalized, and dual-kernel verified within days of Anthropic’s October clique-evaluator release.
